summary:
What did you develop?
We developed SPACE ODYSSEY, a browser-based, single-player 3D-2D educational space-exploration game. Players choose one of three missions: Space Station, Moon Landing, or Mars Exploration. They move an astronaut and press E near a glowing object to record a discovery. The page also shows mission objectives, life-support, power and shielding indicators, and an educational radiation-watch panel. It is built with JavaScript ES modules, Vite, and Phaser 3, with scenes, player controls, mission data, resource state, and the HUD kept in separate modules that communicate through game events.
How does it address the challenge?
Space science can feel distant and abstract when it is only read from a textbook. SPACE ODYSSEY turns it into hands-on exploration. Instead of memorizing facts, students move through a mission, discover objects, and watch the resource indicators and radiation-watch panel, which introduce real space concepts through play. Because it runs in a web browser, there is nothing to install, so it is easy to start.
Why is it important?
Interactive learning makes science more approachable and engaging. Our modular design also makes the project easy to extend. It is currently single-player, with no multiplayer or live NASA data yet, but future versions could add multiplayer, a verified live science-data source, and more missions.
